title: Multi-view CNN predicts pediatric obstructive sleep apnea severity from facial photographs
summary: A multicenter retrospective study of 212 children with frontal and lateral facial photographs linked to polysomnography built a three-class model (non-OSA, mild OSA, moderate-to-severe OSA) using a multi-view convolutional neural network (MVCNN). In the internal evaluation (149 patients) MVCNN reached macro-AUC 0.898 (95% CI 0.863-0.930), macro-F1 0.839, balanced accuracy 0.840 and accuracy 0.846, exceeding ResNet-50 by 0.061 in macro-AUC (95% CI 0.022-0.106; P = 0.004). An external cohort of 63 children was also evaluated, but its numbers were not visible in the abstract.
ai_technology: Multi-view convolutional neural network (MVCNN) on facial photographs

evidence.tested: Internal (n=149) and external (n=63) patient-level evaluation against polysomnography.
evidence.unknown: External performance values; prospective use; full text not reviewed.
